name: Prince Mohammad Bin Abdulaziz Airport
before:
Medina's airport, fourth busiest in Saudi Arabia, handling 10,912,802 passengers in 2024. Along with Jeddah it is one of the two points at which pilgrims enter the kingdom, and it takes charter traffic during the Hajj and Umrah seasons.

The terminal is worth knowing about for its own sake. It was the first commercial airport terminal anywhere in the Middle East or North Africa to earn LEED Gold certification from the United States Green Building Council.

It was a first in another way too. The airport was granted international status in 2007 and the 25-year concession signed in October 2011 was Saudi Arabia's first full public private partnership in aviation, built at a cost of 1.2 billion dollars and named Middle East infrastructure deal of the year in 2013.

The original airport dates from the 1950s and had two runways until 1986, when the second was closed and later turned into an apron.

It is named after Mohammad bin Abdulaziz, the first governor of Medina Province.
after:
Medina's airport, which handled 10,912,802 passengers in 2024. Large numbers of Hajj and Umrah pilgrims use it.

The terminal is worth knowing about for its own sake: it was the first commercial airport terminal anywhere in the Middle East or North Africa to earn LEED Gold certification from the US Green Building Council.

It was a first in another way too. Under a concession signed in October 2011, it became the first airport in Saudi Arabia to be built and run by the private sector, in a project costing 1.2 billion dollars.

FCDO advice against travel in Saudi Arabia covers only the Yemen border area and the cities of Abha and Khamis Mushait. The FCDO also reports Houthi missile and drone attacks on cities and airports across the kingdom since 13 July 2026, and tells British nationals in the Middle East to be prepared for flight cancellations and periodic airspace closures.
